The official AO* author index gives2002 while GSMRL v2 cites2004; original-body/pagination identity remains unresolved. The official adaptive-submodularity v5 comment reports a correction to Theorem13 with additional conditions; neither its revised proof nor a guarantee transfer is claimed. S31. Evidence lineage and units of inference

The historical evaluation lineage remains exposed. The Hydraulic studies repeatedly reused one rig and 421 evaluation cycles after earlier inspection; neither a chronological gap nor a newly frozen selection file creates an independent final sample. The later MHEALTH release recorded a local access boundary for two previously unparsed target participants, but its 527 windows and subsequent wave analyses still share those people and observations. More masks, predictions, scenarios or publication waves increase calculation records, rather than independent participants.

The preserved library begins with the v5 four-page source, followed by the v12 extended manuscript and v13 conference restructuring. V14 audited objective choice and a tuple-copy output ceiling; v15 broadened the output class; v16 jointly selected predictor and mask; v17 learned small gates; v18 and v19 retained the exposed-data setting while adding diagnostics. V19.1 changed reading diagrams, v20 separated main and supplement, v21 strengthened dominance checks, v21.1 repaired display encoding, and v22-v24 refreshed the argument. These publication version numbers are not autonomy wave numbers. [C01-C04]

The registered HAR, Gas and MHEALTH studies form the immediate empirical lineage of the autonomy campaign. The W1-W42 receipt inventory records accepted bounded results, an accepted failed result, operationally blocked starts and unattempted project slots separately. Carrying an earlier paper through another wave does not mean ProbeFlow executed in that wave. Accepted intake is a provenance/lifecycle fact, not scientific approval. The supplement and timeline preserve every wave status without replacing scientific history with operational incidents.

W44 adds two semantic witnesses, not two application datasets: the static witness reuses mask 5 of one previously stored seven-coordinate W41 environment, and the deadline witness uses two acquired IDs in four constructed bit worlds. The original eight static rows encode four distinct conjunctions twice; the eight deadline rows apply two schedules to the same four worlds. The author's sixteen raw-only checks and a separate coordinator arithmetic review reuse these observations. No row, recheck, saved policy or new document version adds an independent participant. S32. What the Hydraulic lineage established and failed to establish

The three-channel Hydraulic replay first exposed a support failure: restoring marginal training labels did not restore useful selective coverage, and 391 of the 421 evaluation joint conditions were absent from the training prefix. In v12, removing a centroid prior offset reduced full-source component error from 0.723872 to 0.473872, with the entire 0.25 change confined to the cooler head. The selection-chosen nearest neighbor tied that full-source score. Under raw-sample prices TS1 matched full-source error at quote 60 rather than 6660; under equal source prices the selection-locked choice lost to a simple source/order control. These are exposed within-program observations. [C02]

The tuple-copy premise gave the v14 ceiling of 30/421 complete-vector successes. V15 permitted class-balanced per-head neighbor voting at k in {1,3,5,11,31}; it generated 25,000 prediction records and matched all 5,000 prior k=1 records. Selection still chose k=1, preserving all nine price-budget choices. An unselected k=3/mask3 diagnostic composed ten train-unseen tuples and reached 40/421 complete successes. This escapes the copying premise rather than refuting its conditional ceiling or validating the unselected model. [C03]

V16 joint predictor-mask selection changed three equal-price decisions but the strong TS1/k1 control still had one fewer component error. V17 fitted 390 gates on 102 policy-fit cycles, selected on another 102 cycles and evaluated 90 dependent settings on the same 421 exposed cycles. Its primary selector retained fixed PS1; a forced TS1-first gate matched TS1 component error while spending 22 extra quotes. Six k3-gate selections included four component improvements and two regressions, and all policy-fit targets shared one joint condition. V19-v24 then narrowed the conditional obstruction: the primary two leaves ultimately had identical four-head predictions on all 421 cycles, so any common prediction-label loss agrees and extra acquisition only adds nonnegative price. A secondary gate saved 63 component errors and 324 quotes while adding ten vector failures. No single aggregate turns that tradeoff into general utility. [C04]

S33. Controlled HAR, Gas and MHEALTH observations

The HAR study fit on 14 participants and 4,996 windows, selected on seven participants and 2,356 windows, and evaluated the official nine-participant, 2,947-window test split. No candidate met the primary development error threshold 0.10, so the primary selected policy was null. A secondary cap-two gate reduced macro error by about 0.514 percentage points relative to strong fixed A while increasing mean quote from 1 to about 1.08127; its paths matched the same-STOP fixed order, three participants had worse error and four had worse secondary objective. The now-exposed test cannot become a new independent final for later edits. [C05]

The next Gas study opened batches 8-10 once under its joint release: 4,364 measurements, 3,277 errors and 4,364 quotes gave exact J=4369/5455. Routing and the strongest myopic policy both bought G4 and immediately stopped on every measurement. Their contrast was zero and the second-action denominator was zero. Naming a controller adaptive did not create adaptive behavior. [C06]

The same frozen predictor and the same development opportunities belong to the simple baselines as well as the proposed controller. MHEALTH routing, myopic acquisition and an ordered prefix executed identical target actions, and all 129 routing second decisions used the sparse-state unconditional fallback. The route-minus-strongest-baseline participant-macro contrast was exactly zero. Retaining the fixed G3+G4 policy with zero target errors at a higher logical quote exposes an objective tradeoff; it does not permit replacing the preselected primary comparator after release.

MHEALTH used subjects 1-3 for fifteen RF mask fits, subject 4 for temperature selection, 5-6 for action gains, 7-8 for policy selection and 9-10 for evaluation. The four positional groups were chest acceleration, ECG, ankle and wrist/lower arm, not four independent devices. The group definition avoided inferring the unresolved physical identity of duplicated/missing README axis entries. The 128-row nonoverlapping admission rule yielded 267 and 260 target windows. A sole frozen bank was shared with ChronoSense, making those projects dependent analyses of the same data. [C07]

The selected development policy had all 252 second decisions in G4; the target route likewise used G4 in all 129 second decisions, with 398 G3-to-STOP windows. The joint release explicitly permitted descriptive evaluation after the development support failure; it did not waive the adaptation-claim gate. Participant 9 supplied all 22 routing errors, all class 2 after STOP; participant 10 supplied none. Full-access RF had zero errors across 527 windows, while the full-access centroid had 34/267 and 22/260 errors. Those full-access diagnostics lie outside the cap-two policy contest and demonstrate neither conditional-routing gain nor clinical validity. The original outcome remains insufficient_support. [C07]

S35. From identified intervals to a fixed minimax information design

W14 replaced a homogeneous-window shortcut with nonuniform window boxes, unequal participant sizes and a single shared cap B on unknown requested errors. It computed 3,636 cells; macro and pooled endpoints differed in 3,506, and copying the full cap to every participant was nonsharp in 912. Informative cells still included 974 no-gain outcomes, and 672 scenarios were infeasible. W15 made the query subset a decision variable fixed before readings, evaluating eight constructed designs, 368 subsets, 3,726 transcripts and 73 budget decisions. Information improved the specified worst width in 44 decisions and tied in 29; these are design choices, not new participants. [C13,C14]

In the current declared world model, participant j has n_j windows, requested set A_j, known stop-error set E_j and other stops O_j. Requested binary errors u share sum(u)<=B; u=1 on E and zero on O. Route availability r and static availability v are independent within-participant box/mean polytopes, each with sum n_j/2. For request indicator A, c=1/20 and k>=0, route loss is (1-A*r)u+c(1+A)+kA(1-r), static loss is (1-v)u+2c+k(1-v). Delta averages the per-participant differences. Querying coordinate i returns a guaranteed closed bin [0,t_i] or [t_i,1] for v_i. The bins overlap at t_i and the implementation preserves that semantics. [C08,C13]

The endpoint oracle minimizes and maximizes Delta over compatible original worlds. At fixed requested errors, each availability term is linear on a box intersected with one sum constraint: fill lower bounds, then allocate remaining mass in coefficient order. Enumerating local binary placements and convolving exact error counts across participants preserves one global cap. Independence of the declared participant/policy availability sets permits concatenating optimizers and hence sharp endpoints; it is a model assumption, not a discovery about real failures.

A change in a fixed program can explain a change in that program without identifying a physical mechanism or a population effect. The Hydraulic scoring-offset contrast, the MHEALTH RF-versus-centroid diagnostic and the finite availability models answer different controlled questions. None identifies the causal effect of purchasing a real sensor reading, corrects unknown physical metadata, or supplies the independent clinical or industrial utility evidence that the original acquisition motivation still requires.

S36. Integrated procedure and module boundaries

The observation-dependent part must be stated precisely. An acquisition policy may react to revealed feature values, whereas the minimax query selector commits to its entire subset before any bin reading. Its internal enumeration of hidden losses supplies an adversarial bound, never information disclosed to the policy. Wave 42 deliberately compares these policy classes and shows that adaptive early stopping can change expected paid price even when final error, worst price and worst conditional width remain tied.

The integrated scientific procedure has an empirical observation layer and a robust-design layer. The empirical layer freezes predictor/development access and evaluates observable paths and failures. The robust layer consumes only a validated public model of the unresolved quantities; it does not read an unobserved fallback prediction as though it had been measured. The sharp endpoint routine, prefix traversal, optional envelope allocator and budget selector have distinct contracts. Saved raw records support a separately written original-loss arithmetic audit. [C08,C15-C18]

Operationally the preserved studies use source/contract seals, exact owned output directories, single-attempt stage records and explicit failed, unknown, impossible and unstarted states. A source mismatch, malformed public field, infeasible box, resource breach or ambiguous call is retained, rather than silently repaired or retried. Those local guards are cooperative code boundaries; timeout and path checks are not OS security isolation, external preregistration or scientific certification.

The terminal-permutation adapter is a representation boundary between an ordered tuple and an ID-keyed reading, not a new acquisition planner. It validates identical unique-ID subsets, reindexes every full label, preserves impossible/feasible status and all ties, and leaves the original action and solver diagnostic records untouched. In deadline or history-dependent settings it returns a failed static-assumption comparison instead of applying the quotient. [C23-C26]

Algorithm: Integrated ProbeFlow procedure: freeze, observe, identify and design

Require: Frozen predictor and explicit public acquisition/STOP/cost contract; training, development and evaluation access ledger. For robust design only: participant partitions, guaranteed availability bins, shared binary-error cap, prices, budget and exact endpoint specification.

Ensure: Observable policy contrasts and their support/failure denominators; or stated insufficient_support/no_gain. Under the declared world model: exact fixed-subset risks, all worst transcript ties, canonical affordable choice and all affordable primary-risk ties.

1. Freeze predictor, observation rights, loss, aggregation, prices, candidate selection and source versions before the relevant evaluation release.
2. Run only authorized empirical acquisition stages; retain attempts, STOP paths, missing counterfactuals, participant errors and cost scope. A zero branch denominator cannot demonstrate routing gain.
3. Represent unresolved requested losses and availability as explicit compatible worlds; reject hidden outcome inputs and unverified guaranteed-bin claims.
4. For each precommitted query subset traverse feasible bin transcripts, using exact sharp endpoints at leaves and safe outward prefix envelopes only for the inner width maximum.
5. For the shared envelope use exact local-cap allocation by DP or the proved implicit marginal heap. Preserve the separate sharp endpoint routine and per-solver cold-cache rights.
6. Prune only if a prefix upper width is strictly below an already completed leaf incumbent. Expand equality and keep every worst transcript tie.
7. If comparing static orders, validate the common item-ID set and observation relation, then reindex terminal tuples by ID before comparing endpoints/full ties. Keep action order and solver diagnostics as separate outputs; do not apply this step across schedule-dependent feasibility.
8. Apply each hard query budget to the completed risk table; minimize (risk,price,mask) and separately return every affordable primary-risk tie.
9. Audit original-world arithmetic and full output partitions from saved records, retain failed/no_gain/cost-regression results, and state the scope still requiring independent application evidence.

S37. Exactness, safe pruning and why greedy transfer fails

The worst-width information objective does not inherit a greedy approximation guarantee merely because its subject is information acquisition. The preserved complementarity witness has R(4)=R(5)=R(6)=3/8 and R(7)=1/4, so the same added item has marginal gain zero at one subset and 1/8 at a larger subset. A stale zero marginal is therefore not a certified future upper bound. Safe pruning instead follows containment of compatible worlds and preserves equality branches when all worst transcripts are required.

For prefix h and completion z, compatible worlds satisfy Omega_z subset Omega_h. Thus L(h)<=L(z)<=U(z)<=U(h), so prefix width is an upper bound for every descendant width. The largest completed feasible leaf width b is a lower bound on R(S). Cutting only U(h)-L(h)<b preserves the maximum and every maximizing complete label. Equality pruning can lose ties even when the numeric optimum is unchanged. This is an inner maximization certificate, not a lower bound that can discard a subset from the outer minimization. [C15,C16]

W18 verified the complementarity and heuristic boundary on three synthetic cases: 84 subsets and 819 readings, of which 730 were feasible and 89 impossible. A cost-ratio heuristic incurred regret 1/60 on a declared budget trap. W19 preserved 108 subset risks, five budget choices and all worst labels after strict pruning, but fewer feasible leaves (837 to 642) required more endpoint calls (837 to 1370) and more raw node bytes (183,934 to 287,257). A correct bound alone was not a compute saving. [C15,C16]

W21 derived a cheaper outward local envelope, exact at B=0. Endpoint calls fell from 785 to 741 across its four conditions, but two conditions had no endpoint gain and total nodes, CPU and retained output regressed. W22 then made the objective/backup distinction explicit: expected-cost AND/OR search, worst-transcript width search, upper/lower certificates and primary-tie contracts must agree before a solver correspondence is claimed. Its two conditions tied endpoint counts at 17 while prefix nodes rose from 18 to 28. [C17,C18]

S38. Shared-cap dynamic programming and the implicit heap

For each participant the local outward envelope yields a base interval and one correction curve per sign f_j(b)=w_j min(b,c_j), where w_j=1/(P*n_j), 0<=b<=a_j, c_minus=a_j-l_A and c_plus=h_A. W39 combines these curves with sum b_j<=B by exact dynamic programming, tightening the cap-relaxed envelope. It still relaxes local coupling, so its interval is generally not the sharp endpoint interval. The established containment is L_relaxed<=L_shared<=L_sharp<=U_sharp<=U_shared<=U_relaxed. At B=0 the corrections vanish and the base is attainable under the declared independent model. [C19]

W41 observes nonnegative nonincreasing marginal chains delta_j(t)=w_j min(1,max(0,c_j-(t-1))). For each sign, initialize the first positive marginal from each chain in a heap, repeatedly pop the greatest and advance only that chain, stopping after B pops or no positive gain. The selected positive marginals form prefixes and attain the sum of the globally greatest available gains. Any feasible at-most-B allocation chooses chain prefixes and cannot exceed that sum. Therefore heap and DP scalar corrections agree exactly; allocation tie choices do not replace the required transcript/subset ties. This restates the saved theorem, rather than adding a new empirical result. [C20]

W39 used one heterogeneous two-participant, five-coordinate structure and two cap conditions: 64 risks, 486 complete labels and 20 budget decisions. At B=1 the shared bound reduced endpoint calls from cap-relaxed 208 to 201, with the same 480 linear calls and the same single-observation CPU, while strong sharp-prefix caching needed only 121 endpoints. W41 used one three-participant, seven-coordinate structure: 256 risks, 4,374 complete labels and 26 budget decisions across two cap conditions. The ten solver-condition records were complete, but B=2 all thirteen budgets tied the empty subset in risk. These quantities are constructed verification denominators. [C19,C20]

S39. Terminal permutation: a precise invariance theorem

Let I be immutable item IDs, Omega a common nonempty world set, and R_i(omega,b) a static observation relation. A subset M is fixed before any observations. Its order pi is a permutation of M; b is a positional label tuple, while z={pi_j maps to b_j} is the terminal ID function. Define F_pi(b) by the conjunction of all R_pi_j(omega,b_j). Closed threshold bins may overlap: either retain the same relation on both sides or use one identical deterministic boundary rule. Changing the rule with order violates the theorem. [C23]

Theorem (terminal reindexing). For another permutation sigma of the same M define T(b)_j=b_(pi inverse(sigma_j)). T has inverse T from sigma back to pi, and F_pi(b)=F_sigma(T(b)). Hence feasible tuple sets correspond bijectively, infeasible tuples remain infeasible, and the infimum, supremum and width of the same Delta agree. Proof: every item-ID observation atom occurs once on both sides with the same label; conjunction order changes no atom. Substituting them gives both set inclusions. Inversion follows by composing the two positional index maps. [C23]

If all selected items are immediately and always available, are revealed once, and the policy reads all M before a history-independent terminal STOP, additive C(M) and affordability under Q agree. An order-invariant terminal predictor P(M,z) has equal terminal loss. Maximizing width over the terminal bijection preserves R(M) and transports every maximizing label; applying this argument to a common subset family preserves the (risk,price,mask) choice and all affordable primary-risk subset ties. This is a mathematical consequence for the family, not a newly executed all-subset study. [C23,C24]

The empty subset has the unique empty order and tuple, F(())=Omega, price 0 and full worst tie set {()}. An empty base Omega is an invalid model, never a zero-risk observation. If infima/suprema are not attained their equality still follows from equal world sets; the stored finite-binary compact polytopes attain both. A common prior pushed forward along T preserves expected terminal loss across orders, which still does not equate expectation with a worst value. [C23]

In the saved static witness M={0,2}, actual W41 enumeration order [2,0] becomes canonical [0,2]. Positional (0,1) maps to (1,0), both meaning z(0)=1,z(2)=0. Its sharp interval is [-11/90,43/90], with width 54/90=3/5; both price 2. Both z(2)=0 readings are worst ties. The other two ID readings have width 17/30, so the widths are not constant and W42's full-support constant-width bridge is not established. [C25]

The conjunction is invariant only after ID-preserving reindexing under a common static observation relation.

Equal feasible worlds and the same original loss imply equal endpoints, hence equal width and transported complete worst ties.

S40. Action order, solver diagnostics and a deadline counterexample

Three objects must remain distinct: a terminal ID reading (M,z), an acquisition action sequence A, and the solver diagnostic prefix record D. W41's stop-error-first order at research.py lines 216-225 controls static enumeration/label coordinates; it is not a record that sensors ran in that time order. D can contain visits, bounds, incumbent updates, cache hits and strict-prune decisions. Terminal equivalence asserts none of those prefix facts. [C24]

With common reveal/boundary/STOP semantics, equal order functions on reachable inputs imply equal acquisition traces by induction on their positions. Conversely, if all items are acquired and traces preserve IDs, literal trace equality forces the same item at each position. Distinct permutations therefore differ at the first unequal ID, even if the observed labels coincide. Different prefixes can condition on different subsets and yield different bounds, pruning and total work. The theorem does not predict a solver speedup. [C24]

The counterexample changes the environment identically for both schedules: items {0,2}, unit duration and price, hard budget 2, completion deadlines d0=1 and d2=2, four bit worlds and target XOR. Order [0,2] completes at times 1 and 2. Order [2,0] reveals item 2 at time 1, then rejects item 0 before acquisition because its proposed completion 2 exceeds deadline 1. All four [2,0] schedules are infeasible; all four [0,2] schedules complete. The rejected prefix pays price 1 and leaves XOR width 1; completion pays 2 and leaves width 0. Lower incomplete-prefix price is not a successful cheap policy. [C26]

Two IDs are minimal for distinct permutations; one world suffices to show schedule infeasibility. The four constructed worlds additionally show residual target uncertainty and do not claim minimal world count or empirical failure probability. The comparison demonstrates violation of static always-available reveals under a common changed deadline model. It is not an improvement over the original W41 problem and must not be pooled with static width rows as an algorithm benchmark. [C26]

S41. Complexity and measurement limits

Let N=sum n_j, A=sum a_j, b=min(B,A), and P be the number of participants. A conservative sharp endpoint cost is H=O(sum_j 2^a_j*n_j*log(n_j)+P*(b+1)^2) rational operations, with implementation-specific caches. All subsets and their binary readings contain sum_S 2^|S|=3^N complete labels; full prefix traversal has at most 2*3^N-2^N nodes. The full solver therefore remains exponential even when its envelope allocation becomes cheaper. Required complete tie coordinates, copied box keys, DFS frames and serialized raw records have output-sensitive storage costs. [C08,C16,C20]

The shared-cap allocation module uses O(sum_j B*min(B,a_j)) rational DP transitions, O(B) rolling layers and stored local tables. The implicit heap uses O(N+P+q*log(max(2,P))) rational work including aggregation, q<=min(B,sum a_j), and O(P) heap storage. These bounds concern the envelope allocator; the separate sharp endpoint can still enumerate binary placements and use DP. Fraction GCD, products, comparisons and integer bit growth add costs not captured by rational-operation counts.

Single-run instrumented CPU is neither randomized timing evidence nor a throughput guarantee. In W41 B=2 the heap used less observed CPU than DP but more than sharp-prefix, and had larger peak Python allocations and output than DP. No additional pruning or endpoint reduction occurred. Tracemalloc peak is not RSS; logical file lengths are not physical I/O; returned or sampled Fraction bits do not bound every temporary product. Zero-rounded short-phase CPU means below timer resolution, while missing measurements remain null/unknown. [C20]

W42 review found two remaining complexity gaps: the written O(K*m^2*h^2) policy-audit bound omits the nonzero stop-only h=0 branch, and the claimed Omega(K*T) storage does not distinguish shared child objects from complete serialized tree lengths. This synthesis withdraws those expressions as general validated bounds; it does not claim to repair them with a new theorem. A revised account must separate explicit serialized length sum from shared in-memory objects, original-world scans and arithmetic bits. [C22]

For already supplied valid permutations and fixed-length label references, the new reindexing operation uses O(1+k) average dictionary operations and O(k) additional references, k=|M|. ID hashing/comparison and copying or serializing variable-length labels have their own bit/byte cost; writing L bytes costs at least Omega(L). Enumerating 2^k binary tuples, computing endpoints E(Omega,M,z), rational arithmetic and diagnostic output remain separate. The empty tuple still incurs validation/call work. This local bound does not repair the W42 h=0 policy-generation or shared-object/full-serialization issue. [C28]

S42. sequential-objective analysis: sequential prediction and fixed-subset width are different tasks

The saved GSMRL body describes acquisition and terminal prediction loss. W42 inspected 98,206 selected source bytes and 132 math nodes, with zero alttext/TeX mismatches. The reviewer also read an additional header interval, giving 100,488 bytes in the union. This establishes the recorded extraction and reading scope, not correctness of 132 mathematical statements or identity to a particular publisher/arXiv edition. Printed Equation 1 is per-instance; expected undiscounted loss is the author's explicit MDP interpretation with gamma=1 and no shaping. The original AO* paper and the 2002/2004 identity were not directly established. [C21,C22]

The saved conditional translation matches worlds, feasible observations, prices, hard budgets and precommitted subset policies. It additionally bridges terminal loss to conditional width g(S,omega)=W(S,x_S(omega)); this changes a prediction target when encoded as regression to zero. Under a fixed full-support distribution, E[g]=max W for a given subset if and only if every feasible transcript has constant width: every term p_t(max W-W_t) is nonnegative and their sum vanishes only when each gap does. Alpha=0, a common hard budget, the same secondary lex rule and separately retained complete primary ties then support the restricted value/tie correspondence. Positive additive price can destroy unequal-price primary ties. Maximizing over all distributions restores a maximum but changes the problem. [C21]

The W42 review required a narrower execution claim: W41 orders known stop-error coordinates first and then indices; W42 uses increasing-index canonical subsets. The W44 theorem now supplies the explicit terminal permutation map under static assumptions. Literal original-program ordered traces, prefix bounds/prunes/cache/incumbents and schedule-dependent cases remain outside that result. Availability, delay, failure and chronology can invalidate the quotient, as the common-deadline counterexample shows. The original W42 ordered-program equivalence was not established, and the later terminal result does not retroactively close its review. [C22-C26]

Witness 1 has one feature and three worlds: expected priced loss buys A at 3/8, while worst priced loss stops at 1. Fixed-subset worst conditional Delta=y width is 1 for both empty and one-feature subsets. Witness 2 has two features and three worlds: observe A, stop when A=0, otherwise buy B. It has zero error and expected price 3/2, giving 3/32 at alpha=1/16; the best fixed subset buys both for 1/8. Both have worst price 2, zero final error and zero worst width. The eleven public policies, six subset tables and 51 original-world arithmetic checks are exhaustive finite witnesses, not trained GSMRL, a replay of W41, or new empirical samples. [C21]

The W42 expected-versus-worst and adaptive-versus-static witnesses retain their original objectives and arithmetic after W44. S44. What the cumulative evidence supports

Equal component weights, fixed quote coefficients and worst interval width are declared research objectives, rather than elicited stakeholder preferences. A policy can reduce component errors while worsening complete diagnoses, or reduce expected quoted price while leaving worst price unchanged. The cumulative record therefore keeps target-specific failures and denominators beside each favorable contrast. Clinical safety, participant benefit and industrial utility require evidence beyond the selected scalar objective and remain unmeasured here.

The evidence supports completed local observation contracts, exact conditional numerical contrasts, finite counterexamples, and saved theorem arguments for a declared robust world model. It supports several negative conclusions: no admitted MHEALTH routing gain, no new information at unmeasured fallback cells, no generic submodular guarantee, no objective gain over a matched exact solver, and no consistent total-cost advantage of pruning/DP/heap variants. It also preserves specific theoretical gains, including sharpness outside the failed slack shortcut and tighter shared-cap envelopes, with their domains stated. [C07-C22]

The six W42 review areas remain dated evidence: architecture and finite same-information baselines existed; algorithm correspondence, complexity, application evaluation and related-work version matching were partial. The new ID-preserving terminal quotient answers one narrowly stated semantic question. Literal original-program execution equivalence, stop-only/shared-object/output complexity, independent measured acquisition utility and original AO* primary/version comparison remain needs_evidence. A source hash, accepted Task, terminal theorem or new manuscript does not close those scientific questions. [C22-C29]

S45. Saved feedback, limitations and the next decisive evidence

The saved current-review distribution concern remains active in this cumulative edition. A one-rig exposed Hydraulic result, a two-participant MHEALTH result and a constructed multi-participant fixture have different support. They cannot be pooled into an independent final study, and repeated wave publication does not create a new physical unit. The later theory explains what assumptions would identify an answer; it does not supply the missing independent population or physical-acquisition observations requested by that review.

The saved current-review baseline concern is answered by preserving its negative result rather than selecting a more attractive diagnostic. Hydraulic v15 still admits k=1 and its unchanged nine price-budget decisions; MHEALTH routing still ties the strongest selected myopic rule; shared-cap DP and heap still match the same exact risks and ties. Unselected predictor gains, altered objectives and lower counts for one internal operation remain separately labeled and cannot replace the admitted comparison.

Historical Big Guy highlights in the local library are publication-based editorial interpretations of public writings; the named scholars did not review this work. The newer v15 current-review links point to actual saved Codex review issues PF15-DISTRIBUTION and PF15-BASELINE, authored in a separate lane of the same native session, with their stated audit scope. This edition maps those saved concerns to new exact paragraphs and preserves the original attribution limits. Generic companion reading marks are not feedback, and no new professor, external or model review was commissioned.

A decisive application study would first define independent participant/device units, frozen predictor and information rights, true availability/failure/latency and cost receipts, and a loss chosen for the intended user. Strong static, same-STOP myopic and permitted adaptive controls would share data, tuning opportunities, budgets and outputs. Missing/failed/unknown/no-gain records would remain in denominators; physical and model costs would have explicit scopes. Until those contracts and observations exist, actual acquisition/model evaluation is not_started with cost null and science_status needs_evidence. The cumulative edition preserves completed work without claiming that the remaining research is complete.

The combined contribution is a traceable boundary between completed local evidence and remaining inference: an explicit shared-source/disclosure design, exposed and registered negative application results, sharp assumption-dependent identification, exact fixed-subset selection with complete ties, and a terminal invariance theorem whose deadline counterexample marks its domain. None of these converts an unchanged strongest baseline, unobserved fallback, higher retained cost or invalid schedule into an admitted practical gain.

S47. The action-local rule and its conditional theorem

At the fixed public state the first group/action0 has been acquired, mask=1, spent=1, remaining=1, total=2 and cache is empty. Let F be feasible next actions1,2,3. Each action's frozen fitting leaf supplies a mean loss reduction mu_a and support metadata. S contains only actions with at least30 fitting windows and two fitting participants. With one-quote actions and lambda=0.05, choose the smallest-index supported action maximizing mu_a-0.05 only when the maximum is strictly positive; otherwise STOP. Empty support and nonpositive fitted gain have distinct reasons. [C32]

The blanket ablation applies this same choice only if S=F, otherwise it STOPs. Thus both rules coincide when every feasible action is supported. When some action is unsupported but a different supported action has positive fitted value, only local admission can buy. Every local purchase is supported by construction and at most one additional quote is used. Its fitted incremental value max(0,max over S of mu_a-0.05) weakly exceeds the blanket rule's value; there is no implication for realized prediction error, rare-event safety, population risk or true acquisition value. The local myopic control independently sorts the same values under the same support/STOP/tie rules and therefore defines the identical decision map.

Support-gated fixed subsets1,3,5,9 retain only their one predetermined optional action and buy it when supported, with no positive-net requirement and no replacement. Fixed orders[0,1],[0,2],[0,3] additionally require positive fitted value under multipliers0.5,1,2. All16 policies share the model, first acquired group, attempt cap, information and support lookup rights. This limited fixed-prefix catalogue is not the original full-budget policy class. Thirty-four incompatible static policies, representing17816 paths, were unexecuted and must not be scored as zeros.

Algorithm: One-remaining-quote action-local admission

Require: Frozen73-input RF and fold0 conditional trees; public acquired group0 values/mask1; spent1,remaining1,total2,empty cache. Feasible actions1,2,3; per-action fitting leaf counts/participants; quote1,lambda0.05; lower-index tie rule.

Ensure: STOP with empty-support/nonpositive reason, or one supported extra action and a final frozen prediction; complete cost/intent/trace records.

1. Validate model/input hashes, public mask, dimensions and budget; mismatch fails without a new inference attempt.
2. Encode only acquired group0 and observation bits; compute the frozen initial prediction.
3. Look up each feasible action's conditional leaf using public state, retaining its fitting window/participant support and mean.
4. Build S using each action's own30-window/two-participant predicate; do not veto one supported action because a different action is unsupported.
5. If S is empty, STOP insufficient_support. Otherwise select maximum mean minus0.05 with smallest action-index tie; if value<=0 STOP nonpositive.
6. Before a positive purchase, validate remaining quote/control/time, write intent, copy only the selected local group, debit quote and compute final prediction.
7. Write and flush the trace, check finalization barrier and preserve all failures/unknown states; do not retry an interrupted accepted path.
8. Compute label-based scores only in the evaluator after selection. Keep full-bank/raw-label audit rights separate and retain myopic equality and stronger static controls.

S52. Exact preference sensitivity of a frozen hydraulic gate

This restores the substantive preference derivation from the older detailed supplement, not merely its topic label. The comparison fixes secondary gate g301/k3 versus locked fixed mask3, equal source prices (1,1,1), cap2 and the same421 exposed evaluation cycles. No policy is refitted or selected for a new preference. Alpha weights complete diagnosis against mean-head loss; lambda weights the separately normalized source quote. They are independent decision parameters.

For cycle i and mask m, d_i(m) is an integer number of wrong heads in0..4 and v_i(m)=1 when at least one head is wrong. Component loss is d_i/4; vector loss is v_i. Their convex mixture expresses a preference: alpha0 values each head equally, alpha1 values complete-diagnosis success. It does not transform four dependent head decisions into four independent samples.

Each source quote is1 and a mask may cost at most2. Therefore the mean cost term divides total quotes by3n; the component term divides total wrong heads by4n and the vector term divides wrong cycles byn. In this continuation only, the cost normalizer3 is fixed by the equal-price contract. Replacing it by another price book without changing the derivation is invalid. Lambda cannot authorize an action outside the cap.

The fixed mask3 has924 wrong head decisions,381 wrong complete diagnoses and842 quotes. The unchanged g301 has861,391 and518 respectively. Their signed differences are-63,+10,-324. Component improvement and complete-diagnosis regression are simultaneously true; neither cancels the other before a preference is declared.

Multiplying the component change by1-alpha gives(-63+63alpha)/1684. The vector change is10alpha/421=40alpha/1684. The normalized cost change is-324lambda/1263=-432lambda/1684. Adding them yields(-63+103alpha-432lambda)/1684. The103 coefficient therefore combines63 lost units of component emphasis and40 units of complete-diagnosis penalty; it is not a fitted regression slope.

The zero set isalpha=(63+432lambda)/103. Withlambda0 it is63/103; withlambda1/20 it is423/515. Below the boundary the frozen gate has lower scalar loss, on it the losses tie, and above it fixed mask3 has lower loss. Atlambda5/54 the line reachesalpha1; beyond that cost weight g301 has strictly lower scalar loss for everyalpha in[0,1]. At the threshold onlyalpha1 ties.

Although the gate wins these weighted comparisons at sufficiently large lambda, it still does not dominate the three-coordinate outcome vector: its vector-error coordinate is worse. Cost preference has compensated that regression, not removed it. If one chooses the arbitrary numerical diagonalalpha=lambda, the same algebra gives(-63-329alpha)/1684<0; this one-dimensional slice is not a reason to identify the two parameters or to select them using evaluation outcomes.

The phase diagram evaluates the same two locked outputs everywhere. Its cells are dependent recalculations, not60 separately trained policies or60 independent trials. Policies chosen by a new alpha/lambda-specific fit/dev search would be a different experiment, requiring a new locked candidate-selection protocol and independent evaluation.

S54. Prospective transfer roles, failed attempts and constrained policy selection

This is a prospective implementation contract, not executed PAMAP2 acquisition. After verifying the actual Protocol archive and rights, order eligible participant IDs by a fixed label-independent hash. For nine eligible participants assign the first three to predictor training, next two to policy fitting, next two to development selection and final two to reserved test. Thus the earlier five fit subjects are split into disjoint 3+2 roles. If inventory or activity support differs, stop and amend before test access; these planned counts are not a power calculation.

Fit normalizers and the mask-aware predictor or fixed per-mask predictor bank only on the three predictor-training subjects. Freeze them before fitting selectors. The two policy-fit subjects supply acquisition/risk training examples; development selects among predeclared candidates and test is opened once for final reporting. Do not silently refit the predictor on five subjects after policy selection. Any such refit is a separate named intervention with its own controls.

The primary task uses nonoverlapping 256-sample completed windows within one Protocol subject/session and one activity-label segment, after raw-time continuity checks. Exclude label0 transition segments from this conditional offline target and retain their counts. Label-based curation defines an evaluation subset; a deployed actor cannot use that gold label or future segment boundaries to choose acquisition. Online prefix inference needs a separate causal windowing contract.

Before fitting, verify internal column names for 16g acceleration xyz and gyroscope xyz in each physical hand/chest/ankle IMU. The proposed minimal representation is per-channel mean and population standard deviation over the completed window: twelve summaries per acquired IMU. Exclude heart rate, Optional sessions, orientation, temperature, magnetometer and redundant acceleration range in this primary interface. Do not invent column offsets before the bundled specification is admitted. Stop rather than adapt features after viewing test outcomes.

For this initial complete-group interface, a requested group is unavailable if any chosen raw channel has an invalid timestamp/sample or missing value inside the window. Retain the failed attempt and its quote. No pre-purchase complete missingness mask, unrevealed summary, activity label or subject identifier is an actor input. A static catalog of the three eligible IMU units is public. Only a charged purchase returns the selected unit summaries or its unavailability indicator. Repeated purchase of an already attempted unit is invalid; STOP costs zero.

The primary caps are one and two attempted IMU purchases. Charge one simulator quote even when the requested group is unavailable; define C as the raw attempted-purchase count in quote units, without division by three, consistently with the main tutorial equation and across all caps/policies. Lambda has units of error per quote; changing the cost normalization requires a corresponding lambda rescaling. These are declared proxy units, not measured energy or wall-clock savings. All-three features are an over-budget reference at caps one/two, not a feasible baseline. Include the zero-purchase predictor prior and every fixed subset feasible at each cap.

Train all selectors against the same frozen predictor and the same two policy-fit subjects. For fixed global GREEDY, use the equal-subject attempt-marginal table defined in S26 on a common mask-eligible row set for each S. Failures contribute zero error reduction, remain in the denominator and cost one quote. This global comparator ignores current purchased values and past failure identities when estimating gains; a conditional selector is a different candidate. Account for every offline target-generation read and fitting cost.

Freeze a common candidate/tuning inventory before development selection, including zero-purchase prior, all feasible fixed subsets, the fixed GREEDY rule and the proposed adaptive selector. Bound training passes, seeds, hyperparameter proposals and selector-compute budget. CAFA-ML or BRiG-AFA is a native comparator only under its pinned classifier, unmasker, budget and data protocol; plugging its acquisition rule into this shared-predictor sensor-group interface is an explicitly adapted comparator. Do not merge the native-system and controlled shared-predictor lanes.

For the single-label primary target use alpha=0. The proposed error cap epsilon=0.10 applies to equal-subject mean development error, not worst-subject error or a population guarantee. At each hard cap k, the predeclared feasible set contains candidates with development equal-subject error at most epsilon, no hard-cap violations, and complete failure/cost accounting. Choose minimum equal-subject attempted cost among feasible candidates, then lower development error, then a predeclared simplicity/order key. Do not use reserved-test labels for ties.

If no candidate is feasible, record no_feasible_policy and keep every candidate failure and excess-error distance; do not silently choose the least-infeasible candidate and claim constraint satisfaction. Lambda values 0,1/20,1/5 define separately labeled preference-sensitivity analyses, not a post-hoc way to relax the primary constrained decision. Report equal-subject mean, every subject, worst subject and pooled-window counts; the last two are diagnostics, not covert alternative selection objectives.

Uncertainty must respect subjects rather than treating overlapping or repeated windows as independent subjects. With two proposed test subjects, show the full per-subject table and refrain from broad population or deployment guarantees. Actual eligible groups, archive identity, missingness, fit, policy choice, native baselines and independent transfer remain unobserved.

Maintain an attempted set T and a successful-observation set S separately. Every attempt increments cost and T; only a valid returned complete group augments S. Query the frozen predictor by S, never by T. At STOP, use the same empty-observation prior, trained on predictor-training subjects with a prespecified class-ID tie rule, if and only if S is empty; otherwise predict from the successfully observed set S, retaining earlier successes after any later failed purchase. Keep their classification errors and consumed cost in every window/subject denominator. No policy may drop unavailable windows after seeing its own acquisition path.

For fixed global GREEDY use S26, not success-conditional mean gain. Maintain successful-observation set S and attempted set T, rank only j outside T, and use the same S-indexed gain table after failures. Positive ties use the declared hand/chest/ankle order. STOP for nonpositive gains or exhausted cap. A reached state with an undefined fit denominator is not_estimable and falls back to STOP with its current valid prediction, never zero gain imputation or row deletion. S26 states the limits of this deliberately history-blind table.

Participant assignment uses predeclared structural admission and a label-independent ID hash, never model outcomes or test class frequencies. Apply the fixed label0/transition curation after assignment and log every resulting window count. The equal-subject formula is defined only if every planned evaluated subject has m_s greater than zero. If any dev/test subject has zero retained windows, record not_evaluable with the original planned subject denominator; do not drop, impute zero error, replace subjects or claim the original reserved test remains untouched. This differs from no_feasible_policy, which requires defined metrics and no candidate meeting the fixed constraints.

S55. Attempt-marginal global GREEDY with common eligible windows

This section defines a prospective comparator; no PAMAP2 archive was acquired and no selector was fitted. Let S be successfully purchased units and T all attempted units. The actor sees S, T, purchased summaries, remaining cap and a previously fitted table; it receives no current unpurchased availability mask, values or labels. The executor alone resolves a purchase and charges one quote even on failure.

For each planned policy-fit subject s and mask S, I_s(S) contains all prespecified retained policy-fit windows where every group in S is valid. Use this same set for every candidate j outside S; do not additionally restrict it to successful j purchases. A_sij records whether j would return a complete valid group. The after-loss is evaluated only when A=1. Failures retain the prediction f_S, so their error reduction is exactly zero, not an excluded denominator. The empty mask includes every prespecified retained window. Offline target construction may inspect policy-fit labels and availability, with its full collection/compute cost recorded. Define d_sij(S) as the before-minus-after loss on success and exactly zero on failure; the after-loss need not exist for a failed return.

Define m_s(S)=|I_s(S)| and average each subject first, then subjects equally. If any planned subject has m_s(S)=0, the whole S table is not_estimable. Do not drop that subject, replace its mean by zero or change the subject count. At a reached unestimable state, STOP using f_S (the frozen prior only for S empty), keep its error and attempted cost, and separately count this fallback. Do not claim the table was estimated.

This is a global mask-indexed baseline. It does not condition the gain table on current purchased values or the identities of failed earlier attempts. Correlated failures can therefore make it suboptimal. All rows where S is valid are used instead of rows selected by a fitted test policy. There is no causal transport, unbiased on-policy utility or optimality claim. A T-conditioned or observation-conditioned acquisition rule is a separately fitted and budgeted candidate.

Choose the unattempted unit with largest strictly positive g(S,j); break ties by hand/chest/ankle. Attempt it, increase T and cost, augment S only on a valid return, then repeat within the hard cap. Nonpositive best gain, no remaining unit, exhausted cap or an unestimable table causes STOP. The unit-quote rule makes raw-error gain ranking well defined here; non-unit future prices would require a separate declared ranking or constrained optimization, not a silent gain/price ratio.

Constructed counterexample: candidate A fixes nine of100 baseline errors but succeeds on only those nine windows; B succeeds on100 windows and fixes20. Attempt-marginal gains are9/100 versus20/100, favoring B. Success-conditional means are1 versus1/5, incorrectly favoring A for this declared attempt objective. These are invented arithmetic examples, not data frequencies.

Subject weighting can independently reverse a ranking. With one window for subject1 and nine for subject2, A has gains1 and0, whereas B has gains0 and2/9. Equal-subject gains are1/2 versus1/9, but pooled-window gains are1/10 versus1/5. The estimator must follow the predeclared equal-subject target rather than whichever average favors the selected method.

It checks attempt charging, no repeat purchases, S subset T, failed-return state preservation, tie order, prior-only-when-S-empty and undefined-table STOP. It is a same-author contract check; its trace count is neither independent people nor measured accuracy. analysis/probeflow-v24-results.json and its frozen code document exact denominators and a trace hash.

In the formula, K is the fixed planned policy-fit subject count. For each S, every candidate j uses exactly I_s(S), including j failures; j-specific success filtering is forbidden. Offline target construction is permitted only on the policy-fit subjects under its own charged collection/compute scope. The actor cannot inspect an unpurchased success indicator. After a failed attempt, T grows and S remains unchanged; the same S-indexed table is consulted for the remaining unattempted candidates. A failed after-loss is not evaluated or invented: d is defined as zero by retained f_S, while its quote is still charged.

The40960 count belongs to an already saved same-author synthetic contract check, not a new replay by this edition. Its factors are8availability patterns×256binary frozen per-mask output banks×4caps(0..3)×5gain-table patterns. No PAMAP2 raw acquisition, accuracy result, learned selector, new benchmark or independent participant is supplied by these traces. Algorithm: Prospective global mask-indexed attempt-marginal GREEDY

Require: Frozen predictor f_S (training-only prior for empty S), planned fit subjects, common I_s(S), unit attempted quote, hard attempt cap and fixed hand/chest/ankle tie order. Offline fitted S-indexed gains, initially S=T=empty; actor observes purchased summaries/failures only, never current unpurchased availability or label.

Ensure: STOP plus valid f_S prediction or a sequence of charged attempts; distinct successful S and attempted T; complete failure/cost/fallback denominators.

1. For every planned fit subject and successful mask S, fix I_s(S) from retained windows where all S groups are valid, using identical rows for every next j.
2. On successful j define before-minus-after loss; on failed j define d=0 without requesting a nonexistent after-loss, retaining that window and attempted quote.
3. Average within each subject by m_s(S), then equally over all K planned subjects; if any m_s=0 mark the whole S table not_estimable.
4. At a reached not_estimable state STOP with current f_S (prior only if S empty), retain prediction error/attempt cost and count this fallback.
5. Among j outside T, choose strictly positive maximum g(S,j), ties by fixed physical-unit order; STOP when cap exhausted, no candidates or no positive gain.
6. Attempt j and charge one quote regardless of success; add j to T always, to S and purchased summaries only on a valid complete return.
7. Continue with the same S-indexed table after failure. No repeated purchase, hidden availability read, subject dropping, zero filling or policy-dependent row filtering is allowed.
8. Retain all declared evaluation subjects/windows; an empty dev/test subject is not_evaluable, distinct from a defined feasible-set search returning no_feasible_policy.

All candidate actions share each S-indexed eligible-window denominator. If any planned m_s(S)=0 the entire table is not_estimable, not zero.

Abstract

ProbeFlow examines when additional acquired information improves a frozen predictor and when incomplete observations support only a bounded conclusion. We connect explicit acquisition/disclosure accounting, negative controlled prediction studies, sharp partial identification and exact fixed-subset information design. These are separate estimands, not one pooled benchmark. Conditional proofs establish sharp endpoints, strict full-tie pruning, a shared-marginal heap and static terminal reindexing; they do not establish real acquisition utility.

The most recent saved comparison uses16 policies on524 already exposed development windows from two participants. Action-local support admission corrects16 errors within41 guard-changed windows, with25 error ties and0 local harms. The candidate nevertheless ties local myopic on every paired window, harms39 initially correct windows overall, and has higher macro error-plus-quote loss than strong fixed subset/order controls. No untouched final groups remain. We restore exact preference and support-stratum diagnostics and a prospective failure-inclusive GREEDY denominator contract. This edition performs source synthesis and saved-data arithmetic, with no new fit, inference, acquisition or efficacy experiment.

1. Introduction and bounded contributions

Buying a source, computing a statistic and disclosing it to a decision policy are different events. ProbeFlow starts from that accounting problem and asks a stricter question before adding planning: can a frozen predictor use the permitted information better than a strong affordable fixed or myopic rule? The cumulative application record frequently answers no or insufficient_support. Its later identification theory states what follows from declared missing-outcome and availability assumptions; it does not repair a failed application comparison. [C01-C07]

Our contributions are bounded: (i) an explicit public-information and charged-attempt contract with preserved negative comparisons; (ii) sharp original-loss bounds and exact pre-observation subset selection under a specified world model, including every primary and transcript tie; (iii) a proof of static terminal reindexing with a common-deadline counterexample; and (iv) a paired descriptive assessment of action-local support admission against its ablation and stronger matched controls. None claims nonmyopic benefit, physical cost savings, population safety or external-method superiority.

The main paper follows problem, theory, experimental setup and results. Full teaching, assumptions, data admission, EDA, failed executions, proof details and chronological evidence remain in the supplement and55-chapter Korean guide. Every previous body section has one canonical retained location, recorded separately from new synthesis. Edition-specific claims inside historical chapters are dated historical statements; their filenames refer to the frozen source inventory unless the new coverage map supplies a successor.

2. Related work and scope of comparison

Joint active feature acquisition/classification [shim2018] motivates set encoding; generative-surrogate acquisition [li2021,gsmrl-local-primary] models sequential actions, STOP and prediction. Our fixed-subset worst-width design instead selects all queries before readings. Matching a name or set notation does not match the objective or policy class. Chronological action masking in the saved time-series source prevents a general transfer of static order invariance.

Adaptive-submodularity guarantees [adaptive-submodularity] require structural assumptions not proved here; a stored complementarity witness violates diminishing returns for this worst-width objective. Repeated selection requires evaluation discipline [cawley2010]. Original AO* body/version identity, including the2002/2004 citation conflict, remains unresolved [inherited-author-index]. No native GSMRL/AO* benchmark was reproduced.

Reference reading is bounded and inherited from the separately saved verifier: official metadata/abstracts and specifically identified GSMRL or Shim opening passages, not full-paper/proof/code reproduction. UCI metadata identify the MHEALTH dataset [uci319], not local physical-axis correctness or clinical validity. The seven reference scope records and exact source hashes remain intact.

3. Problem, information rights and objectives

A prediction actor receives only purchased public values, observation mask and allowed support metadata. The executor tracks attempted versus successful acquisition, quotes and failures; the evaluator alone reads gold labels after decisions. Internal source/cache state and public disclosure are distinct. The current same-process implementation is a cooperative interface, not OS isolation. One logical quote is not measured energy, latency or money.

Current prediction policies share a frozen mask-aware predictor, first acquired group0, optional actions1..3, one remaining unit quote and total cap2. The primary descriptive objective averages each participant error and quotes first, then weights participants equally with lambda=1/20. All planned subject denominators must be positive. Pooled windows answer a different question.

The separate identification task fixes subset S before reading guaranteed closed bins. Compatible original worlds give sharp [L(S,z),U(S,z)] for route-minus-static macro loss Delta. Risk is the largest conditional interval width. Select the affordable lexicographic risk/price/mask representative and separately return every affordable primary-risk tie. There is no learned prior over readings and no observation-dependent subset change. [C08,C13-C20]

E_s and C_s are integer error and attempted-quote totals. P=2,n7=266,n8=258 in the current exposed comparison.

This is worst identified width under a hard logical query budget, distinct from expected prediction loss.

4. Method and executable decision contract

At mask1 each feasible optional action has a frozen fitting-leaf mean loss reduction mu and its own support. Admit an action only with at least30 fitting windows from two fitting participants. Select the smallest-index supported action maximizing mu−0.05 if that maximum is strictly positive; otherwise STOP, distinguishing empty support from nonpositive gain. An unsupported alternative does not veto another supported action. The blanket ablation requires every feasible action to be supported before applying the same selection.

The independently implemented local myopic rule sorts these same net values under identical support, STOP and ties, so it defines exactly the same one-step decision map. Fixed subsets buy their single prescribed optional action when supported, without requiring positive fitted net value. Fixed orders additionally apply the specified multiplier to the positive-net test. All16 current arms share predictor, public input, support rights, unit quotes, cap and524 paired windows. They are a limited fixed-prefix catalogue, not a complete full-budget external comparison.

For the robust-design branch, traverse feasible readings of each precommitted subset with exact sharp endpoints and strict certified prefix pruning. Shared-cap DP or the proved marginal heap tightens only the outward envelope; it leaves the sharp oracle and all output ties intact. The integrated algorithm and full proof are retained in the supplement. The prospective mask-indexed GREEDY comparator has its own common eligible-window and failed-attempt contract; it was not executed in the current16-arm study.

Algorithm: One-remaining-quote action-local admission

Require: Frozen73-input RF and fold0 conditional trees; public acquired group0 values/mask1; spent1,remaining1,total2,empty cache. Feasible actions1,2,3; per-action fitting leaf counts/participants; quote1,lambda0.05; lower-index tie rule.

Ensure: STOP with empty-support/nonpositive reason, or one supported extra action and a final frozen prediction; complete cost/intent/trace records.

1. Validate model/input hashes, public mask, dimensions and budget; mismatch fails without a new inference attempt.
2. Encode only acquired group0 and observation bits; compute the frozen initial prediction.
3. Look up each feasible action's conditional leaf using public state, retaining its fitting window/participant support and mean.
4. Build S using each action's own30-window/two-participant predicate; do not veto one supported action because a different action is unsupported.
5. If S is empty, STOP insufficient_support. Otherwise select maximum mean minus0.05 with smallest action-index tie; if value<=0 STOP nonpositive.
6. Before a positive purchase, validate remaining quote/control/time, write intent, copy only the selected local group, debit quote and compute final prediction.
7. Write and flush the trace, check finalization barrier and preserve all failures/unknown states; do not retry an interrupted accepted path.
8. Compute label-based scores only in the evaluator after selection. Keep full-bank/raw-label audit rights separate and retain myopic equality and stronger static controls.

5. Theory: conditional guarantees and failure boundaries

Action-local admission never buys an unsupported action and uses at most one remaining quote. Its fitted incremental value weakly dominates blanket by cases: when all feasible actions are supported they coincide; otherwise blanket contributes0 while local contributes max(0,best supported net). This is a fitted-value statement. It supplies no realized error or population-safety dominance; the observed39 harms demonstrate the distinction.

For exact design, compatible-world containment gives L(h)<=L(z)<=U(z)<=U(h) for every completed descendant z of prefix h. A completed feasible leaf supplies incumbent b. Prune only when the certified prefix width is strictly below b; equality must be explored to preserve every worst transcript. The shared-cap correction has nonnegative nonincreasing marginal chains; repeatedly taking the largest exposed chain head attains the best at-most-B allocation. It agrees with DP scalar bounds, not a new application result. [C15-C20]

Static terminal theorem: under immutable unique IDs, a common nonempty world set, the same static per-ID observation relation and fixed subset, ID-preserving tuple reindexing is a bijection with identical feasible worlds and endpoints. Immediate always-successful reveals, common terminal STOP, additive price and no chronology restrictions extend this to cost and terminal prediction. Literal action traces, prefix diagnostics, cache/incumbent behavior and work are not preserved. A two-item common-deadline construction violates the static assumptions and yields0/4 versus4/4 completions, not an algorithm benchmark. [C23-C28]

The solver remains exponential: all subset/binary-reading pairs total3^N. Heap bounds concern its local allocator, with rational bits and output length separate. Stop-only work, shared child objects versus serialized policy length, full deployment and physical acquisition costs remain unresolved. The non-submodular witness and stronger exact controls prevent a generic greedy or total-cost superiority claim.

10. Limitations and conclusion

The evidence comprises exposed local prediction cohorts, declared mathematical world models and finite constructed witnesses. It supplies neither an untouched confirmatory population nor measured physical acquisition utility. Support thresholds are admission counts, not calibrated guarantees. Preference and root-range analyses are post-hoc diagnostics. New source coverage, check counts, page counts and theorem exactness do not turn them into practical improvement.

ProbeFlow currently contributes explicit information/attempt accounting, preserved negative comparisons, sharp assumption-dependent identification and exact fixed-subset design with full ties. Action-local admission improves one blanket-guard contrast locally, while matched myopic ties and stronger fixed-policy regressions remain decisive. A next application claim requires independently frozen groups, prespecified utility, real failure/delay/cost receipts and the strongest feasible controls under common data, public information, tuning and acquisition budgets. Scientific status remains needs_evidence; scientific certification, gate closure, promotion and submission are false.

11. Reproducibility and reporting checklist

Claims and limitations: bounded contributions, negative findings, harms, denominators and missing independent final are stated above. Theory: assumptions and detailed proofs are retained in the supplement. Experimental reproducibility: frozen source hashes, integer counts, public-information contracts and original failure records are linked; this edition adds arithmetic checks only, without executing research code. Statistical uncertainty: no independent-window confidence interval or new population estimate is claimed.

Resources and ethics scope: logical quotes, measured CPU/wall scopes and missing full costs remain separate. Existing licensed-source reading scopes are preserved; no new dataset or participant information is acquired. Code, frozen-model/source and policy identities are supplied by hash; authoring tokens/cost and physical acquisition remain unmeasured. This reporting checklist is an editorial disclosure, not a claim that an official conference checklist, nine-page limit, anonymous review, author identity, submission or LaTeX compliance has passed.

The reading PDFs are to be produced with the pinned existing Typst builder by a separate integration Task. The earlier PATH-only compiler search was incomplete: integration located an existing Tectonic0.17.0 executable. Official-style preprint LaTeX source remains preparatory here; author compilation and venue compliance are unverified. Integration will test the existing cache without network downloads. Separate independent semantic review, actual full-book compilation, per-PDF size/page measurements and all-page visual review remain required before publication.

Question, contribution and evidence status

The question is whether incomplete-log identification sets preserve contextual acquisition gains against strong fixed strategies, and whether risk correction changes the error/cost/harm of a frozen predictor on already exposed development participants. This study implements an actual log→joint completion set→full-policy contrast→gate chain and a separate frozen-forest DEV arm.

The bounded execution and alternative raw-only oracle completed once. Scientific status is needs_evidence. Controlled comparisons have a failure-abstain fixed-control omission; they cannot establish superiority to all eligible static strategies. DEV is two previously used participants, not independent application confirmation.

Information, architecture and trust boundary

Controlled logging, set construction, fixed policy evaluation and evaluator-only truth are separate functions. H is paid equally before selection; one shared potential world determines both policies and query failures. Full trees are frozen before calibration, and a single completion parameter is used across all branches and both policies.

DEV reuses only the portable48-tree forest, source-hashed standard-library NPZ/forest semantics and W48 tokens/thresholds. No parent module, main, pickle or lifecycle is imported. Selector access is cooperative within one process: hidden labels/features and evaluator cache are not passed to it, but no OS security isolation is claimed.

Algorithm and validity conditions

Four known mixture designs generate coarsened labels with independent MCAR retention3/4. Conditional on independent retained Bernoulli samples, Hoeffding union bounds induce one nonrectangular set with four coordinates and at most16 constraints. Unknown coordinates remain ranges; empty/unsupported conditions fall back to reference. The PRNG run illustrates the declared model and does not estimate population coverage.

Exact rational active-set enumeration gives sharp affine paired-loss intervals over this bounded set. Literal per-context lower gating and coupled global minimax enumeration are distinct. No branch-wise nature reselection or post-calibration continuation change occurs.

Algorithm: Log-derived shared-completion certificate for frozen whole policies

Require: Train-only reference and at most32 complete nonanticipating policy trees Independent calibration logs with known mixture and MCAR assumptions; common8-world K Initial paid context, failure/abstain/cost contract and remaining attempt budget

Ensure: Sharp conditional paired terminal-loss intervals and literal gate or reference fallback Same-world terminal metrics, explicit unsupported/empty/failure and limitations

1. Freeze all whole trees and reference using train only; never give evaluator theta to interval/gate functions.
2. Read each calibration outcome/missing event and count retained labels per known mixture design.
3. Intersect simultaneous Bernoulli mean bounds with the four-coordinate unit box; leave unobserved ranges free.
4. Enumerate exact feasible vertices, compute full terminal-loss contrasts in the same potential worlds and optimize each affine contrast over that one set.
5. At supported context choose the largest lower contrast, reference first on ties; return reference on unsupported or empty sets.
6. Execute the selected frozen tree through observed tokens/failures only, charging every attempt and initial context. Do not replan its continuation.
7. Compare literal gate with a separately enumerated coupled root optimum and retain gain/no_gain/regression and coverage failures.

Conditional guarantee and its limits

For Delta_j(h)=E[L_b-L_j|h], the good simultaneous-containment event gives J_gate<=J_b and J_gate-min_j J_j<=B-A. A is the contextual oracle gap over the complete frozen menu; B averages the true best contrast width on supported contexts and M on unsupported ones. A/B use evaluator truth and are posthoc explanatory quantities, not gate inputs.

Let D=E_H[max_j Delta_j-Delta_gate]. Bounded terminal losses imply0<=D<=M=23/20 on all events and D<=B on the good event. Thus expected baseline regret is at most delta*M and expected menu regret is at most E[B-A]+delta*M under the stated sampling assumptions. These elementary bounds do not establish novelty, arbitrary-MNAR/OOD safety or DEV calibration.

Controlled observations and comparator failure

The main stores all1024 complete potential-world terminal records and eight log-derived sets. Narrow/wide true containment, unsupported fallback, inconsistent empty sets and literal/global values pass the alternative exact check. All main conservatism gaps are0; a synthetic unit case separately has gap1/2. A=0 in these menus because they already include contextual trees; this is not an empirical proof that adaptation has no value.

Recorded narrow contextual gain against the declared fixed list is0.075; narrow static-sufficient gain is0.025. Inspection reveals the latter gate is q1_abstainF in both contexts, itself a fixed-order strategy omitted from reference selection. Bit lengths depend on rational input/pivots; word counts do not imply bit or polynomial general-policy complexity. This run is only d4,m<=16,H2,K<=32,W8. Model API calls0, new predictor fits0, native episodes0 and no skill activation. Complete controlled procedure and log events

For each mechanism, train logs use1024 events per design with seed101 or102. Calibration narrow uses4096 per design; wide16; unsupported omits design3; inconsistent uses incompatible deterministic labels. Every original event is retained as an indexed0/1/M character with design weights, observed/positive/missing counts. Hidden mixture component is deliberately absent from the logging interface.

Train mixture means solve theta0=m0,theta2=m1,theta1=2m2-theta0,theta3=2m3-theta1 with clipping. Twenty conditional tree forms are paired over two contexts, all mandatory controls retained and train-ranked pairs fill at most32 frozen whole policies. This is a finite author-defined menu, not all conceivable policies.

Algorithm: Log-derived shared-completion certificate for frozen whole policies

Require: Train-only reference and at most32 complete nonanticipating policy trees Independent calibration logs with known mixture and MCAR assumptions; common8-world K Initial paid context, failure/abstain/cost contract and remaining attempt budget

Ensure: Sharp conditional paired terminal-loss intervals and literal gate or reference fallback Same-world terminal metrics, explicit unsupported/empty/failure and limitations

1. Freeze all whole trees and reference using train only; never give evaluator theta to interval/gate functions.
2. Read each calibration outcome/missing event and count retained labels per known mixture design.
3. Intersect simultaneous Bernoulli mean bounds with the four-coordinate unit box; leave unobserved ranges free.
4. Enumerate exact feasible vertices, compute full terminal-loss contrasts in the same potential worlds and optimize each affine contrast over that one set.
5. At supported context choose the largest lower contrast, reference first on ties; return reference on unsupported or empty sets.
6. Execute the selected frozen tree through observed tokens/failures only, charging every attempt and initial context. Do not replan its continuation.
7. Compare literal gate with a separately enumerated coupled root optimum and retain gain/no_gain/regression and coverage failures.

Failure law, classifier and matching limits

Action1 fails when F1/B0, action2 when F1/A0. Failed attempts cost one quote and consume budget, emit F and may be followed only by the other action. Initial context quote1 and at most two extra attempts enter total loss. Classifier predicts the observed relevant token or0; abstain costs0.4. Both compared policies use the same V and Y law, not independent worst worlds.

The declared fixed catalogue has STOP, abstain, one-query and both orders plus train-value-gated order controls. It omitted the failure-abstain variants in fixed_ids/reference selection even though they were permitted whole-menu trees. That omission invalidates the promised exhaustive strongest-static interpretation. In static-sufficient narrow, the gate is the identical q1_abstainF tree in both contexts. All original values and selection are unchanged; a new Task is needed for a corrected preregistered comparison.

For each nonempty design, eps=ceil(10^6*sqrt(log160/(2n)))/10^6, delta0.05. Intersect0<=theta_k<=1 with max(0,e/n-eps)<=a_g theta<=min(1,e/n+eps). n0 leaves the design unconstrained. This derives one joint set from logs, never a risk interval supplied by evaluator truth.

Each case checks64 conditional intervals; total512 slots include empty-case null endpoints. Every recorded extremizer and literal/global selection matches.

Proof, selection validity and counterexamples

Condition on train-selected reference/menu and independent calibration retention counts. IID Bernoulli sampling with known coarsening and MCAR permits simultaneous mixture-mean coverage by union bound. Containment implies all affine whole-policy contrasts are covered simultaneously even after selecting by those intervals. Unknown logging weights, informative missingness, learned K, non-IID calibration or changed predictor invalidate this argument.

DERIVATION gives Delta,ell,u,A,B,D and the good/failure-event algebra. The fixed-menu minimum includes contextual complete policies and must not be relabeled minimum fixed acquisition order. A0 in all recorded menus is explicitly preserved. Width-only chooses reference because reference contrast width is0; this ablation is therefore trivial no_gain rather than evidence for useful uncertainty minimization.

The supplied branch-coupled unit construction establishes only that literal gate can be strictly more conservative than the coupled optimizer. All actual main gaps are0. The prerecorded flipped truth produced negative regret, while posthoc stored-affine all-zero truth produced positive regret. Both are retained with different evidentiary status; no unconditional safety is claimed.
